what: Q1 Stage 0 fix pass after the adversarial review of stage0/q1-gates@acb3bc8 (infrastructure only: CPU tests, CPU doctor, black-box probes of the unmodified KernelGYM clone in GPU-less containers; no GPU, no confirmatory data)

container.flags: docker run --network=none, no --gpus, NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=void, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='', worktree copy mounted read-only, unmodified KernelGYM clone @3a84417f mounted read-only at /kernelgym

findings.claim: c3 config ids embed 'input_shape[0]', which schema.CONFIG_ID_RE refuses; the worker crashes building rows after the candidate ran and the runner records reject for every kernel on 10 L1 problems
findings.verified: 20 committed c3 ids (U1 and U2 on L1/89, 90, 91, 92, 93, 94, 96, 98, 99, 100) fail CONFIG_ID_RE with their draw and seed suffix; runner.py records a post-load crash as reject
findings.fix: shapes.root_label writes tuple-element roots as 'input_shape.0' (overrides keep the real name); shapes._config refuses an invalid id; manifest regenerated with the same 587/915/865 configurations; gate_c.c_configs checks ids before loading a candidate; the worker writes one 'infra_failure-harness-row' error row when building or serialising rows fails; the runner retries an infrastructure-failed item once; preregistration section 10 states the crash attribution

findings.claim: mutants of audit-rejected parents count as witnessed
findings.verified: acb3bc8 analysis.metrics defined witnessed as mutant tier == reject with no parent condition (analysis.py:257)
findings.fix: analysis.scope_mutants: a mutant is scored only if the same audit tier and policy accept its parent at the same replicate; exclusions counted by parent verdict

findings.claim: ladder composition (reject dominates error, error excluded) makes c's denominators depend on the outcome when a family is unrefereeable
findings.verified: acb3bc8 _conjoin and metrics; gate_c.aggregate marks a family with no admissible configuration as error; the same applies to audit tiers through A2/A3 and FA-share
findings.fix: a c family with no admissible configuration, and an A2/A3 channel with no admissible draw, is vacuous for every kernel of the problem (decided per problem; disagreements listed and not vacuous); tiers.tier_verdicts(vacuous=...); every gate's MS and FRR use the kernels a, b and c all referee; paired differences on that set

findings.claim: several preregistered metrics and procedures have no frozen code; the FRR unit for criterion 3 does not match
findings.verified: tiers.adjudicate_gate_rejection and tiers.precision_only were called only from tests; no weighting, origin or tier breakdowns, calibration driver or c-lite existed; oracle.calibrate_multiplier raised on the inf that an exact reference produces; metrics() counted FRR per kernel
findings.fix: audit/replay.py + scripts/q1_audit_hole_replay.py + analysis.audit_hole_candidates/audit_hole_summary (criterion 4); precision-only flag per kernel and policy; n/k-weighted MS; breakdowns by family, rule origin and source tier; paired differences; audit/calibration.py + scripts/q1_calibrate_audit.py (members, fault ceiling 1024, exact-reference rule); analysis.c_lite_set_cover; marginal and amortized cost; FRR_independent over kernel-family units with criterion_3_FRR_c; cluster bootstrap over problems linked by kernel family (numpy, vectorised); all in analysis_sha256 or audit_code_sha256

findings.claim: mutants of S1 calibration-half parents are scored, contradicting section 3.5
findings.verified: acb3bc8 report_q1_stage0.py filtered mutants only by the dev/test split
findings.fix: analysis.substrate_halves; the report computes primary metrics with mutant_parents = evaluation substrates and a labelled 's1_calibration_parents' secondary; preregistration 3.5 says those mutants are scored only within the 8 GPU-h cap

findings.claim: gate_b.py transliterates parts of unlicensed KernelGYM triton_detect.py while claiming no code is copied
findings.verified: token similarity measured without printing either source (simcheck.py): kernel_name vs _get_kernel_name raw 0.84, identifiers normalised 0.96, longest common run 18 tokens, 7 shared string literals; _record vs _append_capture 0.63/0.71, 5 literals
findings.disposition: fixed in the code; residual licence risk recorded
findings.fix: gate_b.py rewritten from KERNELGYM_SPEC.md by an agent that had read neither the KernelGYM source nor the earlier hook code; spec gaps (which object a capture names, the 'unknown' fall-through, getattr-based method lookup) measured black-box against the unmodified clone on 40 controlled objects and 5 interpreter kernels, all equal; after the rewrite _resolve_name vs _get_kernel_name is 0.49/0.58 (longest run 7, the 6 shared literals are spec-required attribute names) and capture_text vs _append_capture 0.45/0.57; false docstring claim removed; NOTICE and KERNELGYM_SPEC.md record the history; nothing was ever pushed

findings.claim: a candidate can observe the gate id, seeds and the harness at run time
findings.verified: by code reading: the worker argv names item.json (holds 'gate'); channel seeds are public constants; the harness is on PYTHONPATH
findings.fix: preregistration section 12 records it as a threat-model limit with the three mitigations Stage 1 must meet or explicitly waive; Stage 0's harness-derived kernels do not read their environment

findings.claim: b1 hooks calls 2 and 4 of a fresh module, released KernelGYM hooks 7 and 9 after b0; no b2 empty-profile retry
findings.verified: KERNELGYM_SPEC.md itself says b1 runs on 'the candidate module after b0' and step 4 retries an empty table; gate_b did neither; a call-count fixture passes a fresh-module b1
findings.fix: gate_b.kernelgym_b0_calls replays b0's five candidate calls before b1 and b2; profiler_rows retries an empty table once; doctor fixture relu_call_count_switch and hack control call-count-switch (13 activations)
